data.title: Molluscum curette
data.summary: Curettes & extractors · Double-ended curette with a small round or oval cutting loop, used to scoop out superficial lesions.
data.body:
![Molluscum curette](instruments/molluscum-curette.jpg)

_Also called: Molluscum extractor, Dermal curette, Fox curette, Piffard curette_

Double-ended curette with a small round or oval cutting loop, used to scoop out superficial lesions.

## Parts
- Central handle
- Round or oval loop with cutting edge at either end

## Types / variants
- Fox curette - round cutting edge
- Piffard curette - oval cutting edge
- Rein round curette (PPT1)
- Loop sizes 1-10 mm; 3-4 mm most commonly used

## Uses / indications
- Extraction of molluscum contagiosum
- Curettage of seborrheic keratosis, stucco keratosis, verruca plana and actinic keratosis

## How to hold
Pencil (fountain-pen) grip between thumb, index and middle finger, or potato-peeler grip with the handle in the distal interdigital fold of the index finger and thumb as a stable base; stretch the skin with the other hand.

## Method of use
1. Stretch the skin around the lesion with the other hand
2. Engage the lesion edge with the loop
3. Scoop out with a single firm stroke, keeping the curette at an angle to the skin

## Sterilisation & care
Autoclave, hot air oven, 2% glutaraldehyde or boiling

## Viva points & tips
- Two holding techniques asked in viva: pencil/fountain-pen and potato-peeler (seminar p10)
- Curette removes soft lesional tissue preferentially; normal dermis resists
